reviews.author: Mary C.
reviews.text: Trillium never disappoints !   Great family time !

reviews.author: Matthew P.
reviews.text: Great campground! Campsite #39 is huge and right on the lake. Plenty of room for several tents, plus the parking is paved and fairly level for our 20 ft trailer. Lots of space to spread out. Only downside is the trail that goes around the lake makes it a little less private, but a fair trade off for being prime spot on the lake. As far as the lake experience goes, the views are amazing of Mt Hood and the lake is beautiful, but small. Because it is not a very big lake it can get crowded and noisy during peak times. Still perfect for kayaking or paddle boarding, and don't skip out on the lily pad area, it's quite magical. Also, the view of Mt Hood from the day use area at sunrise or sunset are not to be missed.

reviews.author: Matthew P.
reviews.text: Great campground! Campsite #39 is huge and right on the lake. Plenty of room for several tents, plus the parking is paved and fairly level for our 20 ft trailer. reviews.author: Greg  S.
reviews.text: Great site, beautiful lake, facilities were clean  and taken care of.

reviews.author: Melanie  F.
reviews.text:
The fire pits need to be taller to make a warmer fire.
Also we hot super hit by showery weather and got water flowing inside the tent so we had to cut our stay short.

reviews.author: Janice D.
reviews.text: We were in space #25.  We have a 30 ft rv and this site was supposed to be able to accommodate up to a 30ft rv.  The site for one is very narrow, we were able to put out the slide on the right side but unable to put out the awning all the way on the left.  There also is barely enough room to park your towing vehicle in the site.  The campground area was very clean but the surrounding areas of the campsite were very brushy where they had cut trees and brush and just left it there.  We have been camping at Trillium for the last 5 yrs and I will say we will not be booking this site again.  Other than that the lake and views were amazing as always.

reviews.author: Daniel R.
reviews.text: Na

reviews.author: Aaron C.
reviews.text: Great Site!

reviews.author: TIMOTHY H.
reviews.text: Great views from the lake of Mt. Hood.

reviews.author: Margaret S.
reviews.text: Campsite feel very private even with the trails weaving through.

reviews.author: Tracy G.
reviews.text: Great campsite, set back from the road,we couldn't even see any neighbors. Its very roomy, we easily put 3 tents up. I was a little surprised to hear Hwy traffic at night.

reviews.author: Kristina O.
reviews.text: such a beautiful destination. the park itself was very well maintained along with the campsites. our campsite was sizable for tent camping. it had a nice round fire pit. our spot was a bit further away from the lake and even then it was only a 7 minute walk. would definitely recommend!

reviews.author: Lawrence F.
reviews.text: Great campground and beautiful lake!

reviews.author: Teresa S.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake is a lovely place to stay.  The views are phenomenal and the staff keep the place pretty clean. The campers near are were quiet and respectful.

reviews.author: Cassandra V.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake with kayak and paddle board rentals. Pavilion seating was perfectly shaded and in close proximity to lake access while offering privacy.

reviews.author: Nicholas W.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake was great. Although it was bit over cast when we were there, the hikes were very pretty. The campground was nice and clean as well as the bathrooms. The campground hosts were very friendly. I would definitely come back!

reviews.author: Heidi S.
reviews.text: The staff was on point with a quick and easy site swap (away from big dogs). The campground was so clean, quiet, and beautiful. Trillium is our long-time favorite and we were happy to see the place and the experience being well cared for.

reviews.author: Ann H.
reviews.text: Very nice campground. Clean, quiet and a beautiful location.

reviews.author: Hayden A.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake is a very well cared for campground and location. The campsite was big and clean, roads were accessible and in good condition, the trail around the lake is in tip-top shape, it’s in a great location near Mt. Hood, etc. If the campground was full, you’d certainly be around a lot of people, but it’s shaded enough to give a solid woodsy feel and an overall great car camping experience. Bring your fishing pole as the “lake” is very well stocked with rainbows.

reviews.author: Marjie R.
reviews.text: I had a great 2 night stay at Trillium Lake at the end of May. It was really cold and rained the first night but the stay was fun. I walked the 2 mile loop around the lake and got in some pictures of Mt. Hood the first day. With the rainy weather, the clouds covered the mountain for the remainder of my visit. There were a lot of wildflowers and I counted 12 species of birds during my stay. I was also visited by resident squirrels and chipmunks who kept me entertained.

reviews.author: Ashley T.
reviews.text: Beautiful site and amazingly helpful camp hosts. I cannot wait to return!

reviews.author: Emma K.
reviews.text: We stayed at site 043 on 8/26 during our cross country roadtrip. This was a beautiful wooded site very well spaced out from the neighbors with a short secluded walk to the water. We were only here for a short time in the evening and morning but it was perfectly quiet and I would love to stay here again.

reviews.author: Cal S.
reviews.text: Nice, private campsites with easy access to the lake, walking trails, and kayak/paddleboard rentals on the lake.

reviews.author: Amber  P.
reviews.text: Staff was helpful. Campground was clean and we had a great time.

reviews.author: Angela J.
reviews.text:
Too many "helpers" directing everything at checkpoints reminiscent of some socialist "show me your papers" dictatorship -- felt as if we were attending a makeshift carnival hosted by well-meaning, but barley competent amateurs exhibiting the Dunning-Kruger effect; peppered and delivered with equal parts arrogance and annoyed superiority.  

Peace, or lack-thereof, impossible due to "helpers" running about (at all hours) on 4-wheelers; engaging in questionable activities given the number of campers "knocking and asking for help" with limited or no response (from my vantage point observation).

ADVICE: Avoid the "managed" campsites and find a "dispersed camping" area to spike out without outside direction, interference and constant observation.

reviews.author: aanya v.
reviews.text: so beautiful

reviews.author: Bethany G.
reviews.text: Pleasant experience. Helpful, friendly hosts. Nice, clean campground with views to die for of the mountain just a few steps away from the sites.

reviews.author: Gabe  A.
reviews.text: I’ve come up before and it’s been great.  The folks there came and yelled at us about the fire being too big in front of our small children.  We were there after the burn ban had been lifted.  We never left the fire.  We had tools and water.  We were working to get a good coal bed before the very heavy rain came a few hours later.  We removed the larger wood that was not yet on fire and doused it with gallons and gallons of water.  They may have wanted us to douse the whole thing.  Honestly I’m not really sure.  It was a good point that it was partially outside the small rusted out ring sitting atop the ground.  We stopped adding to it and re-centered it inside the ring.  I think it could have been handled much better especially in front of the children.  It was very disappointing.  I am and always have been a steward of the wilderness.    Have a nice day.

reviews.author: Lee Ann C.
reviews.text: Camp site was ready and clean when we arrived. Beautiful setting.  Hiking trails close by. Check in was out on the road.  Camp hosts were not friendly or accommadating. Never saw them out in the camp the whole time we were there.

reviews.author: aren s.
reviews.text: Great time. Lake is gorgeous. Bring something to get in the water. Spot was good and with two parking areas. Lots of trees and right next to the water. The spot is in a culdesac like area of the campground with only 2 other spots. Bathrooms and water are close by. We had 3 tents and a van and ended up putting one of the tents on the end of one of the parking spots because we thought this was a better option then unlevel ground. Nice fire pit and double barbecue pit with a flat cast iron top that we grilled on multiple times. Definitely would go back.

reviews.author: Carolyn C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and lake. Sites are private and well spaced. Trails were nice and in good shape. View of Mt Hood and reflections in the lake were spectacular.

reviews.author: Jenni L.
reviews.text: Large gorgeous site with fabulous views. Quiet. Nice trails.

reviews.author: Merritt Z.
reviews.text: Peaceful and clean

reviews.author: Michele G.
reviews.text:
We stayed in campsite 15 and it’s extremely spacious. Not sure if you are allowed to, but you could easily space out 4 tents at this sight and there’s enough parking space for multiple cars to park at the site as well. There’s also two picnic tables, I assume because one of them is rotting a bit. 
Cell service was good. Very close to the lake and trail around the lake. You get a nice little view of mt hood from this site too! Bathroom and dumpsters are very close but is obscured by the trees around you as well as your neighbors. Beautiful spot. Will definitely be back.

reviews.author: Kimberly T.
reviews.text: We reserved two campsites for a weekend in September for our grown kids, myself and my husband. The campground is organized and clean. The weekend we were there was pretty quiet and great weather. This is the second time we've been to Trillium and we will definitely be back. It's a lovely place. Canoeing on the lake was a highlight.

reviews.author: Amber F.
reviews.text:
The campsites are very large and fairly private, so long as you choose one right off the hiking trail. It is a HEAVILY used day use lake, but still a quiet and relaxing atmosphere. 
The toilets are clean for what they are, but I recommend carrying no your lantern with you even during the day as they can be pretty dark.

reviews.author: John B.
reviews.text: Trillium campground was just as expected.  Kayaking and swimming in the lake was great.  Facilities were well kept.

reviews.author: Robert S.
reviews.text: Outstanding campground! Loved the proximity to the lake, and the walking trails. Terrific views, and very nice campsite. Would definitely recommend this.

reviews.author: Pamela W.
reviews.text: Beautiful area. It was peaceful & relaxing. No showers or flush toilets.

reviews.author: Victoria W.
reviews.text:
Beautiful park with easy lake access. Nice walking paths and excellent view of the mountain.  I really do enjoy this park. 
Parking can be very challenging in the summer, so good to keep that in mind if going on a busy day.
Bathrooms are stinky and gross, which is really the only negative aspect of this park.

reviews.author: Kailyn F.
reviews.text: The campground was beautiful, well kept, and clean.  The communication was  clear and friendly, who definitely stay again!

reviews.author: Jyoti A.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake n roomy campgrounds. Had a great time swimming/kayaking and walking the loop trail. Clean toilets/carry extra toilet paper.

reviews.author: Justin R.
reviews.text: Huge yurt! Three bunk beds and a futon give plenty of space to stretch out. There's no electric lighting or plug-ins, but that adds to the charm. The gas stove kept the worst of the cold out and was relatively straightforward to figure out. No showers but the bathroom was kept in stock. Beautiful place to spend a summer weekend.

reviews.author: DJ P.
reviews.text:
This campground is amazing! I was very happy with my spot and the time on the lake was breathtaking! My spot was a couple deep away from the lake and I think that worked out perfectly. There is a trail that goes around the lake and if you get a spot that is as close to the lake as possible, you are basically on that trail. Being a couple spots deep felt like there was no one near us. Especially nice since you can’t hear the lake either and it can get super busy. The campsites are spaced out well and I liked that the campground has its own ramp access with parking. While we were there, there was a fire ban so unfortunately couldn’t use the very nice looking fire pit. The bathroom was pretty decent for what it is. Everything else was perfect and it was a great time!

We also went over to rent kayaks which was nice and easy. The lake wasn’t too cold so we also swam a bit in it. The only slight negative to the day use side of the lake was that there was so many influencers. It didn’t bother me much at all but it was definitely noticeable. The amazing views make sense for it as well.

reviews.author: Jennifer C.
reviews.text:
Had a lovely time as usual, swimming in the lake, and camping in the clean and private campsites. The only thing that I wish was different is better signage that the loop trail was closed at a section for maintenance. I made the mistake of thinking that the blue arrow trail near the closed section was an alternate trail to the loop. After 10 or 15 minutes I realized I needed to turn around and go back the way I came. It was getting dark and I had to get back to the loop trail, and go all the way back to camp the way I came. A small note that said, 'please turn around and go back the way you came',  would have been more clear. I was not the only person who took the other trail thinking it would get us back to camp, so it was stressful. I have a bad back and the extra long walk exhausted me. Im glad I brought water!  Thanks for an otherwise great weekend.


Jennifer Collins

reviews.author: Cathy J.
reviews.text: A large and popular campground, but the sites are wooded and quiet - private. The lake is the big attraction and it can be full of day hoppers, but there's still room for everyone. The restrooms were clean, as was the whole campground. Friendly staff.

reviews.author: Cathy I.
reviews.text: Breathtaking views, clean campsites, and memories to last a lifetime.  Our family had an amazing time, and we'll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Jennifer N.
reviews.text:
We have been going to Trillium for 40 years. It saddens me to see how "overused" this lake has become. Boom boxes on paddle boards seriously?  Rentals should not be allowed. Entry to day use strictly limited. Perhaps reservations for day use like Multnomah Falls. The water in the lake was actually brown - ick. 
However, the campsite was clean and the pit toilets well maintained. Hosts should be more visible. As we were leaving at 7am one of the groups had a fire 🔥 so much for honoring our national forest!! 
Let's do better next season.

reviews.author: Gregory B.
reviews.text: Trillium is a beautiful campground with private sites. (we had site 17) You can see the awesome reflection of Mt. Hood on the lake. The campsite is adjacent to the 2 mile loop trail around the lake. Negatives are that there are only pit toilets and no hook-ups. Also the day use area is very crowded but they control entry for day-users, so we went down to the lake early in the morning or in the evening. The other issue was that on weekends you had to rent both Friday and Saturday nights which didn't match our schedule exactly, so we rented both nights but did not show up till Saturday which was OK as long as you let them know

reviews.author: Jeremy L.
reviews.text: I had made reservations for 3 different sites for each of the 3 days there. On the first day I was made aware that one site was available for the following 2 nights. So I reached out to a camp host to request a reservation for the available site so I would not have to switch sites 3 times like I originally reserved. He said no and blamed upper level management, which is you, for not allowing the camp host to accommodate these changes. I have a 1 year old baby and would have appreciated being able to stay at a site nearby my family without moving out each day. Then, I was informed that the camp host has the ability to accommodate the request I had made, but chose not to and were unwilling to work with me to make this stay a pleasant one for me. No offense, but I spent hundreds of dollars on the reservations and this feels like a poor return of my investment. Even I was willing to pay extra to cover the new reservation.

reviews.author: NOELLE M.
reviews.text:
Beautiful camp site (27). Though fully occupied, loop was VERY quiet for peak season (early Aug). Lots of butterflies, huckleberries, dragonflies. Restrooms and dumpster had been services appropriately. Only draw back was part of lake trail was closed for repair and there was no signage to indicate until at the closure point.
Overall great experience, look forward to coming back soon.

reviews.author: Qiang L.
reviews.text: Beautiful, natural and peaceful! We are so lucky to reserve here as my family’s first camping experience place!

reviews.author: Jennifer M.
reviews.text: I rented the Group Pavilion for a birthday party - we had a great time!  Great facility and helpful staff!

reviews.author: Ray A.
reviews.text:
I will start by saying we have been going to Trillium Lake for over 20 years. The campground and lake are fabulous even though there are no hookups for my trailer.  The paddleboarding and kayaking are phenomenal. It's sad it has gotten too crowded and the fishing is not like it used to be but we still had a wonderful week.
Having said that I must report a very negative experience involving the main camp host in space #1. He came to our campsite and confronted us about some paper plates in our fire pit. I had put them there to act as firestarters on Monday of that week. On Thursday of that week a fire ban was put on the whole region.  He asked me what I was going to do with the plates. I asked if I could just burn them and he said no and that I would have to get them out. I said OK and as he left he said if I violated the rules again I would be told to leave. I said "excuse me, I don't need to be threatened and that he should show some respect and manners. He said I was arguing with him and my wife and I both said we were not arguing.  Five minutes after he left I cleaned the plates out. The next day he left a note on my truck that accused me of starting a fire the previous night which we did not do. His note was extremely rude and said we were to leave by noon. We immediately went to his space and he came out extremely angry and again accused us of having a fire. I said we never started a fire and he said I was lying. Then he proceeded to use extremely fowl language and started dropping F-bombs on us. He told us loudly in our face to Leave Now!! I told him I wouldn't and go ahead and call the police...I would love for them to come. We then sat down and discussed it and he finally believed us and said we could stay. We left two hours later. I didn't want to be there anymore.  I am 79 years old and have been camping most of my life. I have NEVER been treated like that. This camp host has no business working with the public. He's a very angry rude person. Will never go

reviews.author: Walter A.
reviews.text: Trillium is great and super well managed and well maintained.  My only complaint is how hard it is to get a site and then seeing how many people don't show up for their reservations.

reviews.author: Lance E.
reviews.text: The Yurt was a large space that a group of people could stay comfortably and enjoy an evening playing games or looking at the stars.

reviews.author: Jessica D.
reviews.text: Fantastic campground! Very private sites and good lake access. Should have stayed longer.

reviews.author: Hannah H.
reviews.text: Arrived at sunset on a Wednesday night in July. Easy to find our campsite. Park staff were present around supporting other campers. Bathrooms were easily accessible to our camp site, and clean (even had air fresher in there!) Trail around the lake was, as always, well maintained due to it's frequent use. Sunset from the lake's deck is always a must when I stop by Trillium. In years past I often avoid this campground due to it's busyness, but camping on a Wednesday (even in the summer months), the campground was unbelievably quiet and serene. Thank you to the Park Service Employees for making Trillium a magical place for all to enjoy.

reviews.author: Alex B.
reviews.text: Lovely campground that worked out so well for my first time in Mt Hood. Bathrooms were clean (pit toilets so bring hand sanitizer) and our site allowed for easy access to trail around the lake.

reviews.author: Patrick B.
reviews.text:
Park was very clean and well managed. Pit toilets were also very well maintained. Staff was friendly and helpful. 

Oh, and the lake is BEAUTIFUL

reviews.author: Armelle H.
reviews.text: close to nature

reviews.author: Autumn G.
reviews.text: Beautiful place. Great campground.

reviews.author: jamie m.
reviews.text: A popular but well run CG. You will definitely want to reserve your site well in advance especially if you plan on going during the weekend. Mt Hood is gorgeous!

reviews.author: Maksym V.
reviews.text: Everything is good!

reviews.author: Dan S.
reviews.text: MICE!!!  unbelievable amount of mice.  Might as well have been in a sewer.  As soon as the sun went down the mice went nuts.  They were literally jumping at my legs and feet.  We had to run into the tent and they were crawling all over it.  We ended up leaving.  We felt like we were being attacked.

reviews.author: Teresa S.
reviews.text: The campsite, bathrooms, and the trail around the lake were clean of litter.  We rented a kayak, which was marvelous!

reviews.author: Jeremy M.
reviews.text: Beautiful LAKE beautiful people a tradition I’ve taken a few years off… come and perfect paddle boarding with the view you cannot beat! If only you could make it warmer the night I am there. I would sleep a little better, ha❤️

reviews.author: Kevin P.
reviews.text: Loved it! Great space. Great views. Clean campsite.

reviews.author: Jacquie P.
reviews.text: This is my 4th year in a row going in June. Weather was great and the camp host (woman) was wonderful.  My only concern is the litter that accumulates near the day use areas.  I hiked around the lake several times and am so disappointed in folks leaving behind so much trash - especially plastic bags and containers.  Next time I come up I plan to bring grabbers with me and pick some up. I would have thought the people who charge money for day use permits would take the time to walk the paths and clean up the trash. I absolutely love this lake and camp ground. It has improved so much.

reviews.author: Tracey K.
reviews.text: Clean facilities, large camp sites, beautiful lake.

reviews.author: James P.
reviews.text: Beautiful area, beautiful campground. Bathrooms leave something to be desired, compared to similar units in other State Parks. Fumes overpowering, really dark inside.

reviews.author: Dominick H.
reviews.text: A great campsite, enough parking for 4 ish cars. The site was really quiet despite being right next to other sites which was great. There was a lot of room at the site and the water and bathroom were not too far away either.

reviews.author: Eunyoung A.
reviews.text: The site we stay was very spacious and well maintained. The bathrooms were small and not the cleanest, though, but it was no big deal for us. Other than that, it was an awesome stay. My family really enjoyed paddle boarding in the lake. The water was warm enough even in June and the lake was beautiful.

reviews.author: Jeron C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with wildflowers everywhere.  Looks like the lake is a good place for fishing.  Amenities are the typical pit toilets and water, not fully developed like some other camp sites.

reviews.author: Lenore F.
reviews.text: A quiet, forested campground (early June) with good site privacy and access to the pretty trail around the lake.

reviews.author: Rena S.
reviews.text: Nice campsite. Great weather, but the outhouses were terrible. Full and stunk so bad that they were unusable. Lots of camp hosts riding around but didn't seem to care about the outhouses.

reviews.author: Denise B.
reviews.text: Would have been better if staff would monitor day users from using camp sites and beaches. Way too crowded -possibly limit entries to a manageable number

reviews.author: nicole w.
reviews.text: What a deal! Space for so many people in a beautiful and well maintained yurt. At least one of the beds was memory foam. There were 2 full sized beds, 4 singles, and a futon. We felt so lucky to grab this spot that was probably released from someone who made reservations months ago. Room for improvement: 1. door on yurt did not secure normally, we learned afterwards to “life the door up” for it to secure. A sign would be nice. 2. Our fireplace did not work so we were a bit cold, reported the problem. Otherwise, lovely!

reviews.author: Ian L.
reviews.text: I loved that the camping side was so quiet

reviews.author: Joseph D.
reviews.text: Kayaking was a blast. The site I stayed in was right by the water which was convenient however the down side is you’ll have people walking next to your site for most of the day (heavy foot traffic, not very private). Room for two four man tents comfortably. Bugs were pretty heavy in the evening. Fires were allowed at this time, but not always.

reviews.author: Ken S.
reviews.text: With the weather being close to perfect, our three night stay at Trillium was very pleasant. The park is spacious so it feels like you are really outdoors in nature. The park staff and hosts were wonderful. The people we came in contact with were helpful, happy, and polite. The outhouse was kept clean and attended to daily. I love this campground!!

reviews.author: Thomas G.
reviews.text: Campsites are large with good separation - did not see one campsite that I would not have enjoyed. The campground has its own private boat launch separate from the day use area. The trail around the lake is nice and accessible even for handicapped.

reviews.author: Sheri M.
reviews.text: Camp ground was clean. Large lots with plenty of space between them. Felt like we were the only ones there. Trail around the lake was fantastic! Would recommend to family and friends and will certainly be back.

reviews.author: Brynna F.
reviews.text: We had a great trip. Our spot was the smallest one there, but plenty of space to roam.

reviews.author: Troy B.
reviews.text: Great campground, lots of natural space between sites.   One of the camp hosts could benefit from a 'people skills/cheerfulness' class.   One pit toilet was without odor, the other not so much.   One camper truck with house on top ran their very loud generator all night against the rules.  I think the other 4 cars stuffed into that same site had a discussion with the idiot and the next night was silence.

reviews.author: Tina H.
reviews.text:
One of the employees ran his generator all day every day. He verbally assaulted and threatened one of our campers. 
Nothing was done after having our complaint go to the lead manager. 
They told us he’d be gone that night, not that didn’t happen either. He was allowed to continue to run the generator all day. And each day he wasn’t even at his site to benefit from having it running from early morning to late night.

reviews.author: Thomas B.
reviews.text: Amazing view of Mt Hood and decent amenities. Paved roads and drives for each site. There were a few water taps that were not usable close to our campsite. A minor inconvenience

reviews.author: Pietra W.
reviews.text: Big private camp sites. Beautiful lake and view of Mt Hood.

reviews.author: Nadejda K.
reviews.text:
We had zero issues locating the site. Basically, you just look for the boat ramp and turn left into the small parking lot. The rangers put 4 orange cones with Reserved sign in our parking spots. So super easy. Everyone after the 4th car had to look for parking on the first-come basis, which was somewhat a hassle, but doable.
The large shaded pavilion had 3 picnic tables, a couple benches and an assigned water spigot. Bathroom was nearby.
The site is not directly on the lake, the lake access is probably 20-30 yards down the path. The lake is visible from the site. A short walk away is a boat ramp which make is very convenient for putting in boards and canoes.
This day use site is way more private than the amphitheater one. People are walking by not right through the site like in the amphitheater. 
The picnic tables and benches as well as shaded area are great as well.
The only downside is limited assigned parking and no direct waterfront. So there are pluses and minuses but all in all - great experience.

reviews.author: WILLIAM H.
reviews.text: Loved our site! Camp host was very attentive and kept the toilets clean and sanitized

reviews.author: Max B.
reviews.text: Lots of trees, smallish lake but wonderfully located. Decent cell phone service.

reviews.author: Matthew B.
reviews.text:
We stayed in site 18 and fell victim to the unmarked steep drop off in the parking area which left our car damaged and needing to be winched off of the rock it was stuck on.  This really needs to be marked better and/or a curb to prevent cars from rolling over the edge while parking.
The hosts were great and supportive.

reviews.author: Jeanine W.
reviews.text: We love camping at Trillium Lake. The campsites are big enough. The lake is beautiful and the sky at night is amazing! Watching the sunset on Mt. Hood and star gazing is a must.  The bathrooms were kept clean. There were chipmunks that would run around our site. We enjoyed watching them. We could've done with out the carpenter ants though. This was the first time I've seen them. We took a trip into town for something we needed. I can't wait to come back!

reviews.author: Steve K.
reviews.text: The campground hosts had no control. There were 12 empty spots on Saturday night, why didn’t they make them available? The fee for the xtra vehicle was cash only, no hang tag or proof of payment was given, I was sure they pocketed the money. They tried to tell us only 2 sleeping tents are allowed, never heard that one in the 30 years I have been coming here, we ignored the rule and hosts did nothing. This place was well managed in past years, not so much this year.

reviews.author: Don P.
reviews.text: Awesome, as usual.  The view, water and campsite were exceptional.

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Some lingering trash around common areas after busy weekend. Bathrooms clean and mostly functional.

reviews.author: Jacquie P.
reviews.text: My family and I totally enjoyed our time at the lake.  I love that the trail around the lake has been completed.  The camp hosts do a great job.  Not so happy that dumpster divers went through every dumpster Sunday night around midnight looking for cans and bottles. They made so much noise, but at least they cleaned up after themselves! Campers have been courteous as well. Great place to camp and enjoy the mountain.

reviews.author: Judi C.
reviews.text: Beautiful

reviews.author: Audra L.
reviews.text: Lovely! Toilets smell terrible but that’s to be expected. Lovely camp hosts.

reviews.author: Cristina S.
reviews.text: I have wanted to stay here since I was a young girl. We finally snagged a spot and it was perfect. There was still a bit of snow around, but the campground was very peaceful. Spots are perfectly level and very private and the walk around the lake was beautiful and just the right amount of exercise. The views of Mount Hood are just spectacular and they park host very friendly and helpful. It was really nice being there when it was so quiet as I’m sure it gets very crowded once summer gets going.

reviews.author: Thomas G.
reviews.text: Beautiful area. Great trails. Poorly maintained campground.

reviews.author: SANDRA C.
reviews.text: Very well maintained campground, clean and easy to use.  Walk around the lake was really beautiful.

reviews.author: Eric B.
reviews.text: Although the site was nice and we loved being there, it was extremely irritating that the water was not usable while we were there. There was nothing on the forest service website or the reservation details. We could have planned had we known ahead of time. Instead I get an email the day before we head home.

reviews.author: Simone N.
reviews.text: Reserved the Day Use site for an end of the school year party. There were not clear maps or signs at the entrances to the park on where we should go. We walked around and found a covered picnic shelter, but there were no signs indicating that is was the Day Use site. Another group had set up there and we talked to them about our situation - we had a reservation for a Day Use area and these seemed to be the only structure to fit the description, but they brought up it wasn't marked and couldn't be sure, so we ended up sharing it with them. The site also claimed to come with 4 parking spots, but none were available or marked as going with the Day Use area. Overall, not worth the fee - not easy to find, no ranger nearby to ask for info, not marked, not easy to get to, no clear directions for the group to find it.

reviews.author: Justine A.
reviews.text: Overall, we enjoyed our 2 night stay. It was quiet, spacious, and the outhouses seemed well maintained. Unfortunately, we had to clean up a bunch of scattered trash from the previous users before settling in.  Our first night there, all the water spigots were turned off with plastic bags wrapped around.  No one had emailed about disconnected water, so we had to go back to town to stock up on bottled water. The ranger station knew nothing about water troubles at Trillium, and they recommended we ask the camp host about it. The camp host was not in their designated campsite and was nowhere to be found. Luckily, the water came back on in the middle of our second day there. Be prepared to not have the amenities they say they'll provide...

reviews.author: Glenda K.
reviews.text: Lack of water was challenging. Also there was a LOT of tree debris from winter — on trails, in campground sites, etc.

reviews.author: Danielle B.
reviews.text: Amazing double campsite. Private, close (but not too close) to two bathrooms, and walk down to the lake. Loved it!

reviews.author: Amy P.
reviews.text: The campground has lost some of its charm over the years. The grounds crew who trims trees just leaves the branches and debris on the ground so you have to clean it up if it is in the way. It also seems like a massive fire hazard. The campsite itself was horribly undulated which makes putting up a tent difficult especially if you have more than one tent. Our campsite had three massive holes by the picnic table. They were fixed when we were there but only after we asked. Also, the camp host entered our campsite on more than one occasion without asking if she could come in. She should ask before entering sites.

reviews.author: Nadezhda A.
reviews.text:
While the views were absolutely spectacular, the campground management was nonexistent. We stayed for 3 nights. After showing up, it rained the first night. We looked for the camp host to try and locate some firewood. We walked the ground 3 times, and all 3 hosts' sites had a sign "off duty" on them with no host in sight. We drove 20 minutes to buy some firewood.
On the second day, a host stopped by our site and asked if we needed anything. We explained what happened the night before. She apologized, said that we are lucky that our site looks the way it does because just a few weeks ago we wouldn't even be able to start a fire because our firepit was full of ashes. After that encounter, again, no host in sight for the rest of the trip.
On day 3, toilet paper ran out in all nearby bathrooms and it was clear that they stopped being cleaned on day 3 as well.
We camp a lot, this was the most poorly managed campgound I have ever stayed at in California, Oregon, or Washington states. A shame because the scenery is gorgeous.

reviews.author: Ryan R.
reviews.text: Great spot for swimming, kayaking or fishing. Not a clear lake but still great for swimming. Very nice that lake has no Motor Boats.

reviews.author: Sawyer B.
reviews.text: Trillium campground is PERFECT for access to one of the most popular lakes in Oregon & Mt. Hood. Lots of sites with 1 pit toilet and water per ~10 sites. Sites vary from big enough to support big campers to only tent sites. Fire pit, tent pad,  charcoal grills, and picnic tables all included in each site, no electricity access. Other campers were friendly and mainly kept to themselves, lots of families and dogs. Close to government camp if you need anything last minute!

reviews.author: Simon H.
reviews.text: Slight issue with reservations but hosts were great and found me another spot.  Great campground with amazing views of Mt Hood over the lake.

reviews.author: Timothy V.
reviews.text: Was much better than the last couple of years.  Nice to finally have the trail fixed.  Our campsite was good but a family members picnic table was broken and they complained of bathrooms running out of toilet paper.

reviews.author: Shane L.
reviews.text: We were told the management of the campground changed hands and the previous management failed to winterize the campgrounds, so the pipes burst. Therefore we were without water. The pit toilets were pretty ripe but decently cleaned and stocked. I liked our spot, even tho it was a wee walk to the lake, all the waterfront spots have the a trail running thru them so there is less privacy on those.

reviews.author: Shannon K.
reviews.text:
The lake and campground and hosts were great. Major complaints are the amount of dogs that are off leash mostly from the day use people walking the trail. The dogs run ahead and enter campsites while the majority of campers actually follow the rules. We had over 5 different occasions where dogs came into our site during our stay. While my own dogs were leashed in our site. Also a few campsites thought it was fine to leave their dog off leash in their site but when walking our dog leashed around the road, dogs would run out onto the road from campsite. I understand when people feel their dog is friendly and would never hurt a fly however they don’t know if the dog on leash is not as friendly or may have fear aggression, if everyone could just follow the rules it would have been more enjoyable. 
The camp hosts did the best they could to enforce the leash law but they can’t always see what is going on.

reviews.author: Chris W.
reviews.text: Nice campground, but be aware that there is NO WATER. As of last weekend when we went they were fixing the water lines. There was no notice till you got to the faucet that the water was out.  We had to drive to Still Creek Campground to fill up our water jugs.

reviews.author: Chad B.
reviews.text: The female camp host was rude and unprofessional.

reviews.author: Andrew B.
reviews.text: It's one of the most picturesque lakes I've ever seen. The campground is really nice. The only downside is how crowded it is. To be fair I knew that going in, and we enjoyed ourselves. But if you are looking for a quiet place to camp on a weekend, this ain't it.

reviews.author: Becky H.
reviews.text: I'm pretty new to camping, but it was easy at Trillium Lake. I want to visit again and bring friends.

reviews.author: Sarah M.
reviews.text: Nicely wooded/sheltered sites, clean bathrooms, and easy access to Trillium Lake.

reviews.author: Pascal S.
reviews.text: Allow last minute changes to reservations. Adopt stricter generator rules. 1) allow very limited hours and 2) isolate generator sites to designated loops or areas. They ruin everyone else’s experience! Thanks

reviews.author: Andrea H.
reviews.text: This is a great campground amongst beautiful scenery. My family has camped here many times and have greatly enjoyed it. However, this last trip (Sept. 2023) the management of the campground had noticeably decreased. Generally an incredible place to camp, but maybe not late in the season?

reviews.author: Rebekah N.
reviews.text: A beautiful camp ground . Only challenge was the rain and cold weather . I was hoping  for better weather .

reviews.author: Brian E.
reviews.text: Stunning! Great trails around the lake

reviews.author: Edita G.
reviews.text: One of the better state park campsites I’ve stayed. Beautiful lake within walking distance from the campsites,quiet at night. Loved it!

reviews.author: Maryna D.
reviews.text: Amazing campground!

reviews.author: Jason S.
reviews.text: Very beautiful location.  Staff was extremely friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Mary Ann B.
reviews.text: Overall nice campground. I really wish the bathrooms were maintained a bit better.

reviews.author: Timothy V.
reviews.text: We have been going to Trillium for years and I have to say that it has gone downhill the last couple of years.  Last year our spot did not have a picnic table and this year the picnic table was unsafe to sit on.  There used to be a nice trail around the lake and now you can’t use it.  It seems to me you have more visitors than ever but absolutely no upkeep.  The camp hosts don’t even bother giving you your car pass and aren’t around if you need them. Definitely considering not going next year and finding somewhere nicer.

reviews.author: Dana L.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake great for paddle boards, ect. Large camp sites. Very quiet even though the camp was full.

reviews.author: Marsha W.
reviews.text:
Our picnic at Trillium was absolutely wonderful!.
The facilities were lovely. We will definitely return!

reviews.author: Jackson E.
reviews.text: We had an extremely fun time and our campsite was very clean. We had a great location next to the path an lake. We hiked the path around the lake and we took our paddle boards out onto the lake. Many fun activities to do at the campsite. It was quite unfortunate that there was a no campfire ban in place and we had know way of knowing. I checked the website multiple days leading up to our trip, but it would not say specifics on whether or not there was a ban. This would have been helpful to accurately plan our trip.

reviews.author: Diana K.
reviews.text: We have been camping here for almost 30 years. The decline of management is concerning. We did not see ONE camp host the entire 9 days. The day use users are out of control, COMPLETELY! They are taking over every parking space at the camp side dock area, the beaches everything. It is insane! They are over taking campers on beach areas with no regard at all. There needs to be at the very least signage coming from the day use area trails into the camping area stating CAMPERS ONLY, NO DAY USE. There used to be camp hosts at least controlling this matter some what for vehicles driving into the camping side, No longer. There should also be a controlled limit of vehicles allowed to enter the day use, on weekends ESPECIALLY.  It is wrong for campers paying a good price to not even be able to have a space at the boat ramp and beach area. I really hope this gets addressed, It is out of control.

reviews.author: MELANIE M.
reviews.text: No camp site is on top of the other, each site has great privacy. The bathrooms leave much to be desired, but for pit toilets they were very clean and well stocked. Definitely would recommend! Friends also linited out of fish and we found some huckleberry.  BEST CAMP EVER!.

reviews.author: April H.
reviews.text: Nice place to stay!!!

reviews.author: Candee S.
reviews.text: Park host was very nice and super helpful. We stayed in site #6 on the water. The sites picnic table was broken both benches not attached at all. I had my mom with me who is disabled. Asked several park hosts and rangers for a new table. I was told that it’s the forestry department. This was a super bummer as the table could only be used to store stuff on. They did offer me another site but when I went to look at it #9 the table had holes in it. Would say the site was a bit dirty with trash but I let that go as I knew short staffing. Trillium is one of my favorite places to visit. Another disappointment was how empty the park was most nights I stayed for a week and the sign read full all but 2 nights but on any given night 6-14 were empty. The signs all said reserved. One spot was empty 3 nights. It’s a bummer they couldn’t let others stay in spots that were no shows. Over all it was a great experience. Love love Trillium.

reviews.author: Judi C.
reviews.text: Excellent, clean campground with wonderful camp hosts!

reviews.author: Beccah W.
reviews.text: Lovely camp sites with lots of privacy and easy access to Trillium Lake.  Very peaceful and well maintained.  Potable water, nice little trail around the lake, and friendly camp host.  Only downside was the pit toilets which could use an upgrade.

reviews.author: carlos r.
reviews.text: The camp side was very clean and the host was very professional.

reviews.author: Sarah J.
reviews.text: Lovely park with nice separation between campsites. Beautiful lake with view of Mt Hood.

reviews.author: Mary H.
reviews.text: Absolutely lovely campground!

reviews.author: Pamela C.
reviews.text: Nice shady campsite in a lovely campground. Trail around the lake is easy and pleasant. At this time, there is no where to dump an RV until troutdale.

reviews.author: marci l.
reviews.text: WE LOVED THIS SITE. Contrary to previous reviews we had an excellent experience at PS1 Day - Use site. The site is a covered wood structure with 3 picnic tables up the path from the water and viewing platform on the lake. To get to the site follow the signage (which was excellent from Hwy 26) to the boat launch and park. During our visit the rangers marked off 4 parking spots with our name and pylons. We could not have asked for a better afternoon and VIP treatment. HIghly recommend - just do yourself a favor and review the map then follow the signs, it's an amazing location!

reviews.author: Katie U.
reviews.text: Great campsite, beautiful views, bathrooms were dirty and ran out of TP

reviews.author: JOSEPH T.
reviews.text: Great little campground, easy swim and water toy access. Camp host was pleasant. Neighbors ran a generator far more than we thought was necessary, but that happens sometimes.

reviews.author: Willa K.
reviews.text: Nice big site. Just across the road there is a path that goes along another site to the lake. Very busy on summer weekends!

reviews.author: Mark L.
reviews.text:
It’s nice and quiet. 
They need to update to flushing toilets. Lol

reviews.author: Nell B.
reviews.text: Great campground and great site!

reviews.author: Traci J.
reviews.text: The camp site was overall amazing and the staff were out of this world. The generators are the killer. Wish people knew how to camp/survive without them. Now a days there is solar wish people could just convert. Hate sitting at my camp listening to it and  breathing in the fumes from the campers Nextdoor.

reviews.author: Peter E.
reviews.text: We arrived a hour before checkin. Original site was a bit small for our 2 riggs. We spoke with the host, Brian, who found us a larger available site even closer to the lake. Not our 1st time at Trillium Lake,  but we really enjoyed or 3 day stay again. I hope that the trail and board walks around the lake will be repaired soon. It's taken more than 3 years to do this.

reviews.author: Janice D.
reviews.text: This is our 3rd year of coming to Trillium Lake.  Our first time camping 2 weeks.  We were in the far end of the campground away from the water so we didn't see alot of the people that swarmed the lake over the 4th of July weekend.  But it did make it hard to find a spot to play in the water or fish because of so many people.  The hosts were great and seemed to be right on top of everything.  The bathroom by us was pretty stinky and it ran out of tp a couple times but for the most part it was ok.  My daughter, grandson and I rented kayaks one day and had a great time.  The price point was reasonable.  Fishing was good, weather was perfect.  Looking forward to next year.

reviews.author: Nicole B.
reviews.text: had the perfect little wedding ceremony at trillium amphitheater. it was perfect!

reviews.author: Jeffrey S.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground

reviews.author: Henry M.
reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet campground with great access to Trillium Lake.  Campsites are carved into the tall pines, so every campsite has a lot of privacy.

reviews.author: Jake P.
reviews.text: This was dang near a perfect campsite.

reviews.author: Ronald C.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake is beautiful with Mt. Hood in the background.  Seriously over crowded during 4th of July weekend.  But much quieter and roomier than many state campgrounds.

reviews.author: V M.
reviews.text: What a lovely location for a campground. We had a good site 22, we put our motorhome front in because we could level it easier. The lake is great we loved the view early morning and in the evening. Lots of mosquitos too bad.

reviews.author: Richard O.
reviews.text: Asphalt, small parking, city camping. Go real camping

reviews.author: George B.
reviews.text: A WASTE OF $80 to reserve a group day use site that was unfindable. A campground employee we asked said he did not know where the reserved site might be, nor how we might find it other than, "Try driving around."  Driving around looking for our reserved site proved fruitless.  The BOGUS SITE RESERVATION included four reserved parking spaces which were unfindable.  There was no clear signage at the park entrance to indicate how to find one's way around.  No park personnel were near the entrance to help.  The "Campground Host" was located at a secluded site far from the entrance, and was not available.  THE OREGON PARKS AND RECREATION SHOULD REPLACE THE CONTRACTOR MANAGING THIS PRIME EXAMPLE OF OREGON'S UNIQUE BEAUTY!  As an Oregon resident for 52 years, I'd say the Parks Management is becoming another Portland-like embarrassment for the state's tourist industry.

reviews.author: Riley L.
reviews.text: Awesome campsite right by the water. Spent some time paddle boarding on the lake and walked the trail around the lake. Very scenic and relaxing weekend, would recommend to anyone. Ground keepers were exceptionally nice.

reviews.author: Jacquie P.
reviews.text: My campsite was ready, the weather was wonderful.  I was so happy when by 8PM the area was quiet.  Other campers appeared respectful of others and kept noise down.  I had stopped going to Trillium back in the early 90’s because it just seemed to become a loud party place.  Now, it is back to a nice, family friendly place to go to.  Staff/camp hosts were all really nice.

reviews.author: Lois R.
reviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed this beautiful campground.  The campsites were large and relatively private, the hosts were friendly and helpful, the vault toilets were kept clean, and the lake was a joy to visit.  I couldn’t get enough of the view of Mt. Hood there, and I enjoyed the variety of wildflowers blooming in the woods.

reviews.author: Jay G.
reviews.text: Beautiful site and awesome campground

reviews.author: David F.
reviews.text: Went as planned.

reviews.author: CLAYTON H.
reviews.text: Amazing scenic lake with rewarding rainbow fishing. Very spacious camp sites. It was nicely quiet during my stay and camp hosts were pleasant and helpful. Top of my list for camping and fishing.

reviews.author: Michael E.
reviews.text: a

reviews.author: Alonzo P.
reviews.text: The natural setting of the campground is beautiful; nestled alongside Trillium Lake with the southwest face of Mt Hood as its backdrop.  Campground amenities (vault toilets, potable water) provided for all your necessary personal needs.  Spacing between campsites was more relaxed than many more urbanized campgrounds and foliage between campsites added to a greater sense of personal privacy.  Finally, campground distance from the the highway added to the tranquil peaceful experience easily enjoyed.  Hopefully, repairs to the trail which circles the lake will be completed shortly to complete an otherwise excellent experience.

reviews.author: Adam G.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground helpful staff gorgeous views of mt hood well maintained campsite

reviews.author: RYAN G.
reviews.text: Clean and spacious. Lake was a short walk from the camp ground. It looks like it only goes about 10 feet deep at most, makes it great for kids to swim in and great for fishing in hotter weather. Has a dock to reach deeper water for trout when it's hot. Kayak rentals are available at the second boat ramp. Great views of Mt. Hood on clearer days. Plenty of other lakes and streams around trillium to go to. Bunch of lodges close aswell if you get tired of camp food. Nothing motorized on the lake, very peaceful.

reviews.author: Lisa P.
reviews.text: The sites are all large and private. I had plenty of room to hang my hammock as well as to set up my 8 person tent. The combination of sun and shade was nice. Fires weren't permitted during the time I was there, but my propane fire ring was allowed. The pit toilets were pretty clean for pit toilets, and there were plenty of trash receptacles placed at convenient locations around the park. The access to the boat ramp is great, and the dedicated parking for campers is a great bonus. The trails are nice, and the lake is as beautiful in person as it is in all the pictures. Even if the mountain isn't feeling like showing itself, the view is still amazing. I enjoyed my time here very much and will return for a longer stay next season.

reviews.author: Jennifer C.
reviews.text: My favorite place to camp! But This  trip we reserved site #35, which is a disabled site, for my friend who has a disability. The giant picnic table was blocking the wheelchair ramp, and was too heavy to move. The vault toilet smell was so strong it burned our lungs and we had to wear masks. Normally I have zero complaints about Trillium Lake, we just will not reserve that site again.

reviews.author: Chad S.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake has been a destination for many years. The campground is nicely spread out, and the lake is impressive. Trillium is a fantastic place to spend time with family, friends, or just a couple wanting to get away. The camp hosts are attentive and provide a clean and welcoming experience. Recently, our camp host, Jean, showed outstanding customer service and kindness. We will continue to enjoy Trillium Lake for years to come.

reviews.author: Leslie A.
reviews.text: Quiet, relaxing, beautiful views and large campsite site. Loved it

reviews.author: Anna K.
reviews.text: The prettiest campsite I have ever stayed at. Very secluded, surrounded by beautiful trees. We came late and left early, everything went seamless. The only downside is the vault toilets, and not very many of them per number of campers. However, they were very clean and well maintained.

reviews.author: Patricia C.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake; huge private campgrounds!

reviews.author: Gernot w.
reviews.text: Epic scenery and the campground nicely embedded in the nature

reviews.author: Natalie J.
reviews.text: The location looked very nice but we were unaware of the fire ban when we arrived. We had to leave because we would have had no way of cooking our food so it was a little disappointing, but no one’s fault!

reviews.author: Kristen H.
reviews.text: Great location! The lake is so much fun to take your paddle boards on and your kayaks. The campground is clean and well maintained. Lots of trees for privacy. Great place for families to get away to.

reviews.author: Cassie B.
reviews.text: We have spent this summer staying at campgrounds in Oregon, Idaho, and Washington. Trillium Lake was, by far, our favorite in every way. The campsites were private, yet easy to navigate, the lake and walking paths are gorgeous, the campground was incredibly clean and well-maintained and everyone was incredibly friendly. Our only complaint is that there are lots of places to take garbage, but as true Oregonians, we were disappointed that there was not place to leave recyclables.

reviews.author: Steve P.
reviews.text: Trillium has the most wooded and private sites …… clean portapotties ,excellent trails to walk , nice water valves , beautiful views , friendly people from around the world

reviews.author: Crystal Y.
reviews.text: Loved paddle boarding on the lake but beware of the amount of rocks in the water. They are big, slippery, and some are sharp. I fell and cut my leg up pretty bad. My advice is to have water shoes.

reviews.author: marcie p.
reviews.text: Clean!  Beautiful, spacious tent sites.  Quite day and night.  Perfect experience

reviews.author: Torrey L.
reviews.text: We reserved a day use site for $80 (including fees) so that we would have a spot to be with multiple families. This charge is much more than a camping spot. We could not find the location of the day use site and walked the premise for about 2 frustrating hours, unable to find someone who worked there to help. The spot we were supposed to be at was completely on the opposite side of the part (did not follow the map on Recreation.gov at all) and our name was not posted on the site. The phone number listed on the reservation was a non-working number. There was then no parking in the day use area and the spot was supposed to come with 4 parking spaces. We were told we could go online for a refund but could not figure out how to do so. So we paid $80 for absolutely nothing and cannot get a refund. I highly advise against reserving a day use site. Rent a camp site instead, it will be cheaper and easier to find. Very frustrating, but it was a beautiful day and we made the best of it.

reviews.author: Vasiliy R.
reviews.text: Camp site was nice ,I wish they will build the showers in future

reviews.author: Emily  M.
reviews.text: We had a great experience at Trillium. We loved campsite #56. We'd definitely stay there again. The only problem I noticed were that the large trash bins/dumpsters were very full. I saw people throwing away a lot of recycling and packaging that takes up a lot of space. It might be helpful to post signs about taking recycling home with you and to please not put large items in the trash bins (if this doesn't already exist).  Thank you!  :)

reviews.author: Jessica  T.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful lake and a nice quiet campground. I camped here with my parents and my baby who just turned 1. It was so much fun. The vault toilets were clean. The campsite we had was very private (although it was laid out weird). The roads and parking spaces are all paved which I think helped with the bugs. We brought a double kayak and spent so much time in the water. I would 100% come again.

reviews.author: Alan C.
reviews.text: Great camp site for 2 couples and 2 tents. Had a boat and fished every day. Good fishing and ate trout daily. Some rain but didn't spoil the event.

reviews.author: Megan R.
reviews.text:
You don’t get 4 reserved parking spaces, you get 4 passes and hope your guests can find parking. That was extremely disappointing as I booked the site only because the reservation said we would get 4 reserved spots. There are also no signs pointing you to the reserved day use area, we drove around for 20 minutes before we found it. 

The pavilion was beautiful however and worked well for the birthday party we planned.

reviews.author: Sanna B.
reviews.text:
Pros: This is one of our favorite camping locations. Beautiful forest and that view of Mt Hood from the lake is breathtaking. It is also a great place to set up and then visit Timberline Lodge or spend a day on the alpine slide at Ski Bowl. Also, the toilets were super clean!
Cons: Our picnic table was broken and there was a camp setting off fireworks across the lake late at night. Also, the camping beach access had quite a few non-campers on it. Those are why I gave only 4 stars.

reviews.author: Rahul K.
reviews.text: Well Maintained and close to the lake.

reviews.author: Dawn S.
reviews.text: We reserved spots 17, 19, 26, and 32 for us and several friends. Our friends in spot 32 moved to spot 9 because it was open and pretty much waterfront. Spots 17 & 19 were great- very large and fairly private. Lots of shade and room for several tents. Spot 19 has a large double driveway, enough for probably four vehicles. Spot 17 could house two vehicles. Spot 9 was great for the proximity to the water but not as much tent space and it was sloping down towards the lake. Spot 26 was fine, we didn’t spend much time in it. Overall a great camping experience except for the fireworks, which was annoying but not unexpected. If you get a spot near the lake and main trail, be sure to lock up your stuff. We heard someone had their hammock stolen out of spot 4, which was the spot we decided we would like next time both for size and proximity to the water.

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Campground was clean and well maintained. Hosts are friendly and efficient.

reviews.author: Dana P.
reviews.text: campground was clean and maintained very nicely. The campground was patrolled regularly and we talked to the manager and was very impressed.  Of course the view of the lake was stunning!

reviews.author: Maria Z.
reviews.text: We love this campsite! The location couldn’t be better. Was quiet and it has beautiful hikes around.

reviews.author: Cal P.
reviews.text: We were able to switch our reserved site for an open site (#12A) which was closer to the water. Pit toilets were clean. Nice paved parking spots on sites.Amphitheater near our site was neat.  The rain overnight gave way to amazing views of Mt Hood in the morning reflecting in Trillium Lake. This campground was well worth the stay.

reviews.author: Don M.
reviews.text: It a clean place to enjoy and was glad there is wooded space between the sites. The lake is also very clean.

reviews.author: Brittney S.
reviews.text: The site was very clean and private. Loved our spot! Wish we could see the mountain from where we stayed, but still a great spot.

reviews.author: Jennifer R.
reviews.text: I loved this spot! So beautiful and the spots are really great and mostly private. It was a great experience.

reviews.author: Carly  A.
reviews.text: We had a great time at Trillium. We hiked, paddle boarded and kayaked. The late and its views are stunning. This was our first time there and it quickly became a family favorite spot.

reviews.author: Lily s.
reviews.text: I really enjoyed this location. The restrooms were pretty bad but on our second day of being there they got cleaned. There's no formal check in which was a little confusing at first but I enjoyed my stay. Really pretty place and I loved the trail around the lake.

reviews.author: brandon f.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsites. Lots of room at each site. Easy access to the lake. Pit toilets but in nice clean shacks. Cleaned several times a day. They will let you have a propane fire pit right now. Also there wasn't a standard check in. You go to your site and someone will come around and check you in.

reviews.author: Cindy V.
reviews.text: Even when the day-use area is busy, this campground is quiet and beautiful!

reviews.author: Weining C.
reviews.text: The rangers were nice and the campsite is easily accessible and clean. Two cons: there were loud music / karaoke that disturbed the quiet night 10pm+; also it was a bummer that we can't have fire during the dry season. Overall experience is positive! I wish we could stay longer.

reviews.author: Jordan W.
reviews.text: Paddle board rentals were easy and affordable, highly recommend those.

reviews.author: Nini O.
reviews.text: This is an excellent campground, the sites are spacious and has enough space and trees in-between sites so the campsite will have a private feel to it because you wont be able to see your neighbors. I really like there is a parking area and a boat launch that is away from the day use area for campers. I really enjoyed taking my kayak out during this trip and having the boat launch when I didn't have a campsite right next to the lake made it so much more convenient to take the kayak out. The restroom is a drop style toilet but it is very clean and well maintained. I had a chance to interact the staff to ask them help me find my campsite and check in and they are very friendly. If you're staying at this campsite, watching sunset or sunrise at trillium lake is an absolute must.

reviews.author: akira m.
reviews.text: lovely visit!

reviews.author: James H.
reviews.text: Great camping spots, well maintained with plenty of space buffer between the sites.  While it was full, it didn't feel overly busy.  The lake and view of the mountain are stunning.  No motors on the lake makes for a quiet, relaxing time.  Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Kim C.
reviews.text: Beautiful location, nice facility.  Spacious sites. Helpful staff. My only complaint is that the trail around the lake has been in disrepair for 3 years now.  Some work is being done finally on the wooden pathways but you would think as popular as this location is that repairs would be further along.

reviews.author: jeff k.
reviews.text: Super large camping spots.

reviews.author: David P.
reviews.text: The day use area at this campground gets pretty heavy use.  I does get crowded around the campsites near the lake.  The upside is you'll get wonderful views of Mt. Hood on the south side of the lake.  Take your camera, if you hit it early without a breeze you'll get a great reflection of the mountain off the lake.  I also saw some nice Rainbow Trout taken.

reviews.author: Jeannette Z.
reviews.text: I camped with my granddog. He had a great time swimming in the lake. It was relaxing to watch people enjoy the warm weather, the swimming, kayaking, and being together. Even though you cannot walk the loop all the way through due to repairs, it is very satisfying to just walk each side. I was fortunate that my campsite was quiet. It got so still and so totally dark when it became cloudy at night.

reviews.author: Darien S.
reviews.text: The campground is well taken care of, bathrooms attended frequently, trash receptacles scattered around for easy clean up. We went on a no fire weekend and it was surprisingly peaceful and quiet in the evenings - kind of great surprise for a campground. Nicely sized campsites.

reviews.author: khanh p.
reviews.text:
Water was readily available but vault toilet doesn't have any water hookups ... so the smell was horrible. 
In Summary everything was great except the hygiene issue justified a short stay not more than 2 days.

reviews.author: Suong L.
reviews.text:
When we drove up there were rangers to direct us to our campsite.  047 was a great camp spot near the boat ramp for close and easy access to carry our SUP to the lake. 
Area was clean and good size.
The night that we arrived was super cold and cloudy that hit in the low 50’s to high 30’s and unfortunately campfire was not permitted.  The next morning was clear blue sunny skies and the view of Mt Hood was breathtaking.  Saw a bald eagle the first night and the next morning as well as a Hawk.  Bathrooms are more like an outhouse, but was clean and big.  They had many throughout the campgrounds.  It didn’t seem busy, but maybe it was because it was on a cold weekend.  So it could possibly be busy on hot days.  I reserved my spot several months in advance as it gets booked fast.  Will definitely come back as I enjoyed paddling on the lake with the beautiful view.

reviews.author: Dana B.
reviews.text: Amazing.

reviews.author: Jeanne K.
reviews.text: Thank you for a wonderful camping experience!

reviews.author: Sarah C.
reviews.text: The Lake was beautiful, perfect for kayaking. The tent area was nice and clean, but restrooms were quite smelly. Overall, we loved it and will be returning in the future.

reviews.author: Wendy O.
reviews.text: It a nice quiet park with a great view of Mt Hood.

reviews.author: Frank N.
reviews.text: Rented Kayaks in Clackamas to save money and used them for fishing & cruising. If your camping, try to get a spot closer to the lake so you can easily bring chairs, tubes, coolers etc.  Trees shade is great so there isn’t a need for canopy.

reviews.author: David F.
reviews.text: One of our favorite campgrounds.

reviews.author: Tracy J.
reviews.text: This is a great location. Very enjoyable.

reviews.author: Chris K.
reviews.text: It is family friendly. Bathrooms and faucets at many locations.

reviews.author: Nicole C.
reviews.text: We reserved a lake front tent site for end of July and it was amazing!  Literally just 50 ft from water.  The camp site has walking paths around the lake and around the campgrounds to help people get to the lake easily.  Only negative about our campsite (#6) is that there are a ton of people who walk the path around lake - and you feel a little like you’re on display when you’re hanging out at your site.  Otherwise, campsite was quiet and clean.  We took paddle boards and could drop them in super easily and really enjoyed the lake!  My son gives Trillium Lake a 9/10 for fishing opportunities.  His advice was to “get onto the water with your pole”. (Rainbow Trout).  Take the walking path and enjoy the sites around the lake.  My favorite spot is at the boat ramp and the dock area.  Stunning views.  Also make sure you check out the amphitheater!  Great swimming, fishing and weather for our trip!  Check the weather before you come- but we had highs in high 70s and lows in mid 50s—-perfect!

reviews.author: Judy R.
reviews.text: Absolutely gorgeous campground, our site was perfect with privacy and waterfront access. We would love to return but trying to find availability is so hard. Only downside for us was the immense noise from a group of campers on the dispersed side of the lake which ruined the ambience into the early hours, as the noise carries across the lake. Hoping this was an isolated case as we are keen to return!

reviews.author: Cindy R.
reviews.text: Spent 3 nights here - peaceful, clean campground and had a short walk to the lake from our campsite 56. Bring paddle board or kayak and you can get out on the lake before the Day Use visitors get there! One of the mornings we went up to Timberline Lodge (15 min drive) and after exploring the lodge we took the Miracle Mile ski lift up for $20/person and had amazing views and hiked back down (you can take the lift down too).

reviews.author: Daniel L.
reviews.text: We had a great time. We've been coming to Trillium for years and it's always a great time and the lake is fantastic. Can't wait to come back next summer.

reviews.author: Mark L.
reviews.text: Nice campground. But no fish. ☹️

reviews.author: Kimberly  S.
reviews.text: Pretty spot, need more than one night to thoroughly enjoy and relax as the daily reservation is for less than 24 hours.  Woke to car prowlers looking in my vehicle.  Day use folks walking through camping space was annoying.  Leaving valuables in camp was questionable.   Wasn’t clear what “credentials” to bring, ie printed reservation, forest passes etc.  Clarity of documents required would help.

reviews.author: Gayle D.
reviews.text: Wonderful camp spot, our only concern were the over flowing trash and the restrooms. restrooms needed to be cleaned and kept running out of toilet paper.  This didn't affect us, we had our trailer but other family members had to use these restrooms.

reviews.author: Jennifer  P.
reviews.text: Nice campground with walking paths, ability to access lake with water toys, and breathtaking views of Mt. Hood. Our only complaint was someone running their generator at all hours, but that isn’t the campgrounds fault.

reviews.author: Jonathan L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with friendly hosts. The map is not to scale. We did accidentally book a shared site. Other than that, we had a great time. Loved having easy walking access to the Lake.

reviews.author: steven h.
reviews.text: Immediately upon arrival I found himan feces at my campsite number 23 on 7/12/2021.

reviews.author: Susan M.
reviews.text: Considering how busy & popular this campground is we were very impressed with the maintenance and upkeep. We didn’t see litter anywhere and sour site wasn’t worn out.

reviews.author: David D.
reviews.text: Camp Hosts did a poor job of keeping boat ramps clear of sunbathers and others suggesting there weren’t enough areas for them to hangout elsewhere.  I believe the boat ramps are there to launch boats, canoes, kayaks etc for recreation, not sunbathing. If they needed help the OSP or County Sheriff should have been called.

reviews.author: Minh N.
reviews.text: This was our first time camping at Trillium and it was beautiful. However, the bathroom needs to be upkeep better and clean regularly because the smell was really bad.

reviews.author: Marilyn R.
reviews.text:
Loved the hike around the lake in both directions; great space between campsites, clean and quiet.

The maintenance  staff really cleaned up and raked the sites after a camper checked out.

Very adequate spacing of water spigots.

reviews.author: Tia A.
reviews.text: Favorite place to camp.

reviews.author: Gary E.
reviews.text: Beautiful , Mt. Hood setting! Great outdoors family recretion resource.

reviews.author: Ann K.
reviews.text: Lovely park.  Expect a very busy visit. Day use often has a line of cars waiting for parking spots.  The campsites are kept clean.  Pit toilets are well maintained.

reviews.author: Kimberly G.
reviews.text: Camp hosts were friendly and helpful. Site 21 was well maintained, albeit a little small - better for an RV than tents. Great afternoon shade. The lake is always wonderful. I love that no motors are allowed so paddling around on the water is much more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Melinda L.
reviews.text: Campsite was great but the lake had very little room and was packed with dead fish (for bait) everywhere.

reviews.author: Joshua E.
reviews.text: Breath taking

reviews.author: Jordann K.
reviews.text: Recreation.gov can't control the weather.  That's our only complaint.  Otherwise, it's a great campsite!  Wish we could have seen the sun.

reviews.author: Marharyta M.
reviews.text: Great campground!

reviews.author: Andrew W.
reviews.text: Trillium Lake is quite nice with some gorgeous views of Mt. Hood, great for photographers. Really enjoyed that it's close enough I was able to ride my mountain bike up to Govy and connect with several fun trails, eventually ending back at the lake. The bad? It's unbelievably crowded with people and with large amounts of people comes trash. Seriously, is it so hard to dispose of your garbage responsibly?

reviews.author: Araceli B.
reviews.text:
The hosts were very kind, understanding and responsible! 
Great layout and safety guidelines in place during this COVID era. 

Thank you!

reviews.author: Sharon M.
reviews.text: One of my favorite places since I was a little girl fishing with my Grandpa- now I get to pass on these experiences to my kids!

reviews.author: Peter J.
reviews.text: Great camp site, wish we could light a campfire though. But beautiful view of Mt. Hood

reviews.author: Michael K.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake, kayak and canoe rentals, large private campsites

reviews.author: Bronislav G.
reviews.text: Excellent!

reviews.author: Danielle M.
reviews.text: Very nice that the campground wasnt full!  Woudl be nice if the park rangers/hosts were reasonable about parking in teh driveways.  Seems like they have nothing better to do than ensure that tires are on the asphalt.....while we were there during a fire ban and campsite next to us had a raging fire.  Seems the fire is a bigger risk than a tire 3 inches off the edge.  But they dont go around after dark to see what really goes on....

reviews.author: Takashi D.
reviews.text: Great!

reviews.author: Tara P.
reviews.text:
The view of Mt Hood from Trillium  Lake location was amazing. We were so happy to have been able to rent a Canoe and play on the Lake. So wonderful. 
Only downside- no showers no normal restrooms with soap and sink just vaulted toilets.

reviews.author: Patti F.
reviews.text: Gorgeous site and clean bathroom! We loved our stay!

reviews.author: April A.
reviews.text: Great site location.  Beautiful lake!

reviews.author: Carrie T.
reviews.text: So much busier this year than in years past. Campsites were jam packed with cars and people.

reviews.author: Diana K.
reviews.text: Beautiful place

reviews.author: Elizabeth L.
reviews.text:
The day use area is swamped.  One can tell that the area is boing 'loved to death'. We counted 65 rafts on the lake at one time on a Friday.  The attendants were available and prompt.  Restrooms cleanish.  Why don't campgrounds sell wood anymore?  Thank goodness there was running water.
Beautiful area and the sites are big enough that you can hear your neighbors, but not see them.  The campers are not all 'real campers'.  For example, playing music and being quite loud with their conversations.  City recreationists.

reviews.author: Ruth B.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed many things about this campground. We had a well-appointed campsite, with easy access to water and bathrooms. The fire pit was nice and the picnic table was large and sturdy. The campground was clean and well cared-for. One thing we did not like was the generator noise from the RV in the next campsite over. Also there was no firewood for sale (though there was good kindling around the site).

reviews.author: Mary B.
reviews.text: Great sun and water

reviews.author: Mary B.
reviews.text: Great sun and water destination

reviews.author: Terri R.
reviews.text: A little tight for two bigger trailers as a double site, but made it work

reviews.author: John W.
reviews.text: Very nice and scenic campground located close to Mt. Hood and many hiking trails in the area.  Large campsites that could hold two or three tents.  Highly recommend this campground.

reviews.author: Moe H.
reviews.text: It is a very good place to go. It’s just a little hard to get a spot. But that’s what you have to do.

reviews.author: Walter A.
reviews.text: Trillium is a great place to camp with excellent sites - they are all great.  The main problem is that it is crazy hard to get a reservation.  I wish they would switch to the same platform the state parks use. Don't think to stroll up for one of the walk in sites.  I think people come in on the first day and never leave.  We always see people getting turned away. Bring something to float on the lake with!

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Trillium is such a picturesque place.  We were surprised how large our campsite was, since it was the last one available when we made our reservation.

reviews.author: Kyle F.
reviews.text: Clean facilities, plenty of space between sites, and friendly folks all around. I will be back!

reviews.author: gail d.
reviews.text: We love Trillium. We try to go once late spring/early summer and once in Sept. It is a nice quiet campground with many places to visit close by.  We usually visit Little Crater Lake, Timothy Lake and drive up to the Lodge.  We really enjoy the path around the lake and try to do the walk morning and evening.  We have always had great camp hosts.

reviews.author: Denise B.
reviews.text: Great place to camp and fish with the family. Excellent for kayaking and biking too. The views of the mountain, when it is out, are stunning.

reviews.author: Sydney S.
